audit.title: Send Arbitrary Data
audit.summary: This is a complete, well-structured CCIP tutorial with a fully runnable Solidity contract, concrete addresses/chain selectors, and dense links into API-reference and best-practice pages — best-in-class on code and specifics. Its biggest GEO weaknesses are missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, dates only in body text) and tutorial-style openers that bury the liftable answer, plus a lack of symptom-phrased headings that agents query on. The honest verdict: strong developer content whose retrieval and extraction lag its substance — surgical fixes to answer-first leads and query-phrased headings would move it into the Strong band.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting headings
recommendations.where: new `## Troubleshooting` H2 before `## Explanation`, or H3s under it
recommendations.issue: custom errors defined in code but no heading targets them; only diffuse gas-spike notes exist
recommendations.change: add H3s such as "Why does sendMessagePayLINK revert with NotEnoughBalance", "SenderNotAllowlisted / SourceChainNotAllowlisted error", "My CCIP transaction failed during gas price spikes", each with a one-line cause + fix.
recommendations.why: devs and agents query by error string, not concept; error-titled sections win retrieval that body-text mentions lose.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first TL;DR at the top
recommendations.where: immediately under the H1, before "In this tutorial, you will…"
recommendations.issue: "In this tutorial, you will use Chainlink CCIP to send data…" — framing, not answer
recommendations.change: add 2–3 liftable sentences: "To send arbitrary data across chains with CCIP, build an `EVM2AnyMessage` struct and call the router's `ccipSend` function, paying fees in LINK (`feeToken = LINK`) or native gas (`feeToken = address(0)`). This tutorial deploys a `Messenger` contract between Avalanche Fuji and Ethereum Sepolia."
recommendations.why: gives engines a self-contained, verbatim-liftable canonical answer and names the exact API instead of a generic description.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: measured — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, `dateModified` absent
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-05-19`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, and a `<link rel="canonical">`. Surface the last-updated date as visible HTML too.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T); note this is likely fixed once in the docs template.

recommendations.title: Lead the LINK vs native decision with a comparison table
recommendations.where: top of `## Tutorial` or a new "Choosing a fee token" block
recommendations.issue: the LINK-vs-native distinction is spread across two parallel prose sections
recommendations.change: add a 2-row table: fee token | `feeToken` value | funding step | when to use. E.g. `LINK | address(s_linkToken) | fund 70 LINK | recommended during gas spikes`; `Native | address(0) | fund 1 AVAX | simpler, no approve`.
recommendations.why: lets an engine extract the *reason* to pick each path and build a justified answer.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics
recommendations.change: where a real figure exists, state it; otherwise cut the adjective. "robust, future-proof, and compliant" → "backward-compatible with future CCIP upgrades."
recommendations.why: quantitative/precise claims outperform qualitative prose; vague hedges are neutral-to-negative.

recommendations.title: Add a crisp definition of the message struct near first use
recommendations.where: first mention of `EVM2AnyMessage` in the Explanation
recommendations.issue: struct is used before it is defined in one liftable sentence
recommendations.change: "`EVM2AnyMessage` is the CCIP struct describing a cross-chain message: receiver, data, tokenAmounts, extraArgs, and feeToken."
recommendations.why: gives engines a canonical definition to quote for "what is EVM2AnyMessage."

antiPatterns: Duplicated best-practices/gas-spike blocks repeated verbatim across the LINK and native sections — acceptable for standalone chunking, but adds length without new information.
No unresolved cross-references, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, code is complete with imports — clean.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical URL, and og/twitter tags are almost certainly template-level; fix once across the docs site rather than per page.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; ensure this page is listed there for discoverability.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` on future runs; head metadata could not be verified here, so the metadata score reflects the served-HTML measurement only.
